title: UW External Section Directive 1.0
description: The `external` object replacing a section's payload when that section is held in `.uwpart.md` fragments (UW Composition 1.0 §3, RFC 0021). It names the parts, states how many there are, and — for collection sections — declares which field identifies a row and which field the merged rows occupy. Two constraints this schema cannot express are enforced by the resolver: `part_count` MUST equal `parts.length` (`COMP-COUNT-MISMATCH`), and `collection_key`/`collection_path` are REQUIRED when the named parts are collection members and forbidden otherwise, which depends on the parts rather than on this object.

parts.description: The `part_id`s composing this section, each resolving to a fragment in the same package. Order is not significant: merged rows are sorted by `collection_key` under a byte-wise total order, which is what lets an externalized record digest identically to its inline twin. A repeated id is refused (`COMP-DUP-KEY`).

part_count.description: How many parts compose this section. Redundant against `parts.length` on purpose: without it a truncated `parts` array is undetectable, and a rent roll missing four tenants still totals, still validates, and still produces a confident DSCR. A disagreement is `COMP-COUNT-MISMATCH`.

collection_key.description: Field uniquely identifying a row, e.g. `unit_id`. Required when the parts are collection members. Two fragments claiming the same value is `COMP-DUP-KEY`, never a last-one-wins merge — it is a conflict a human resolves, not an ordering question.

collection_path.description: Field within the section content where merged rows land, e.g. `units`. Required alongside `collection_key`. Digest invariance (I-1) cannot hold without it: the resolved content must equal the inline content exactly, and `units` and `rows` are different documents. Not present in RFC 0021 as originally accepted; added to the RFC by erratum on 2026-08-18 and recorded in UW Composition 1.0 Appendix A.
